text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they often add it to a shared project. A CI system then starts an automated build to check that everything still works. During this process, it also runs tests to find problems. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious. Many companies use CI pipelines, which are a series of steps like building, testing, and preparing the software for release. By using CI, teams can work faster and more safely, because they know that mistakes are found quickly and fixed before they reach users.
